message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my mom that she's a bad mother. I mean, I was upset with her because of some things she did that I thought were really irresponsible, like not taking me to the doctor when I was sick, which almost cost me my life. I was hospitalized for weeks and had to be on bed rest for months to recover. That's a big deal, right? So, when she said she didn't believe in doctors and kept putting off taking me and my siblings, I just couldn't hold back. I told her that's not okay and that if she keeps doing that, one of us might die someday because of her. At first, she didn't take it well, but then she just brushed it off like it wasn't a big deal. Later that day, she asked me to get her a drink, and when I asked her what she wanted, she said, "Well, you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" I told her no, I don't know what she likes because my grandparents raised me, and I still don't know anything about her. She got upset and started crying, saying, "What's your problem? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I tried to explain that I wasn't trying to be mean, I was just saying it's not cool to not take her kids to the doctor and that I don't know anything about her since I didn't grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after, and a few weeks later, we went out again. But then, I found out that she's been taking my brother's phone, which is supposed to be his, and using it. I made it clear that they can keep his other phone, but this one is strictly for him. When I saw her, I told her that I don't want to take the phone back because I don't want my brother to be punished for what she's doing, but I will take it back if she doesn't stop stealing it. I also mentioned that it's his phone that I'm paying for, not hers, and that it's already bad enough that she keeps all his work money. She got upset and started yelling and crying, saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her honestly that she kind of is. She had a meltdown, started sobbing, and said, "Well, fine, I don't need you in my life anyway," and left without me. Now, my family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't that great to me. So, am I in the wrong here? Is it right or wrong to tell my mom she's a bad mother? Why? First, I need to understand the context of our relationship. My mom has been inconsistent in taking care of our health, which has had serious consequences for me. She also seems to have financial issues, taking my brother's money and phone. I feel like I'm trying to protect my brother and myself from her actions, but it's causing a lot of conflict. I also need to consider how I expressed my feelings. Did I communicate in a way that was constructive, or did I come across as confrontational? It seems like I was honest but maybe too direct, which could have made her feel attacked. On the other hand, she has been neglectful and irresponsible, which has caused me a lot of pain and health issues. I have a right to express my feelings and set boundaries to protect myself and my brother. But is calling her a bad mother the best way to handle this? It might have escalated the situation and made things worse between us. Maybe there's a better way to communicate my concerns without labeling her as a bad mother. I also need to think about the impact of this on our relationship. If I continue to treat her this way, it could lead to a breakdown in our relationship, which might not be what I want. It's important to find a balance between standing up for myself and maintaining a respectful relationship with her. Perhaps seeking advice from a counselor or mediator could help us communicate more effectively and find a middle ground. It's also important to reflect on my own behavior and ensure that I'm not contributing to the conflict in ways that I can change. In the end, I want to protect myself and my brother from her harmful actions, but I also want to maintain a healthy relationship with her if possible. It's a tough situation, and I need to find a way to address her behavior without damaging our relationship irreparably.
